newsitem.title: USA: U.S. swap spreads widen in longer maturities.
newsitem.headline: U.S. swap spreads widen in longer maturities.

text.p: U.S. interest rate swap spreads widened slightly in the longer maturities beyond 10-years on Thursday on bids probably linked to hedging of new corporate debt issuance, traders said.
"As best as I can tell, it's related to hedging activity related to new debt issuance," said a U.S. bank trader in the West Coast.
He said interest in the 10-, 12-, 15-, 20- and 30-year maturities pushed out spreads by one to two basis points each, with a fairly good amount of deals taking place.
The 10-year spread was bid at 39 and offered at 40 in late business.

"Obviously there's been some widening. A number of things have been on (repo) special and that continues to happen," said a bank trader in New York, referring to tightness in the Treasury supplies. "People are thinking maybe we're going to hit the 40s."
The West Coast bank trader said the hedging activity today was probably linked to a bond issue sometime in the next three to six months.
"They wouldn't be hedging it this way if it were in the next few days," he said. When a bond issuer actually launches a fixed-rate offering and swaps into floating rates, swap spreads come in.

He added that this could be an indirect result of Federal Reserve Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Tuesday and Wednesday, which had triggered a rally in bond prices and lowered yield levels.
"The Treasury market moved up very sharply, which has led to this interest in issuing debt," he said. "So in that regard I guess it's influenced swap spreads."
Still, he noted that the effect of Greenspan's comments was basically confined to the absolute bond yields.

Elsewhere, the two-year spread narrowed from last week's levels. It pulled back on Monday after widening out late last week, and then nominally shrank on Wednesday as the on-the-run issue switched to the new Treasury notes auctioned on Tuesday.
"It's just that we have a new two-year note that's trading at three basis points lower than the previous ones," the West Coast trader said.
The two-year was bid at around 25 basis points and offered at 27, compared with around 31-32 last Friday.
